records.summary: The look of a control is its appearance; type named it before the axes were split.
sf-alert's look is its appearance, not a variant.
What an alert or a toast reports is its status; type answered that question before the axes were split.
A progress indicator's colour role is its status.
What a component is made of is its kind.
records.manual: sf-tree-item also reads type from its item data (_sourceData.type); write kind there too.

records.summary: What a component is made of is its kind, not a variant.
sf-tag's type answered two questions: a kind (checkbox, icon, color, avatar, default) and a status (info, success, warning, error). Each now has its own axis.
records.manual: Write kind= when the value is checkbox, icon, color, avatar or default, and status= when it is info, success, warning or error.

records.summary: sf-badge's scheme carried statuses; status is the axis now.
records.manual: Move a status value (info, success, warning, error) from scheme= to status=; a colour scheme value stays where it is.

records.summary: Every field takes its size from one attribute, size.
Icon positions are logical, so they follow the writing direction.
Inner spacing is one profile, spacing, with named values.
records.manual: tightness=low becomes spacing=compact, default (or empty) becomes normal, high becomes comfortable, highest becomes spacious.

records.summary: size names the size ladder everywhere; a file's byte size is file-size.
Classes for the gallery's lightbox are lightbox-class; class and root-class belong to the element itself.
The scrollbar's mode is data-mode.
One word for a failure across the Framework: error.
The status without a meaning is neutral; components had their own words for it.
A file preview that picks its look by itself is auto.
A tag with a count is a default tag with count=.
records.manual: Keep the number in count=.

records.summary: The drawer is on the shared size ladder.
Placement is logical, so a drawer follows the writing direction.
records.manual: Only where the page may be right-to-left does the difference show: left stays on the left there, inline-start moves to the right.

records.summary: Context menu positions name a side and an edge in one vocabulary.

records.manual: sf-range-slider-change also fired when a value was set from code; change does not. Code that relied on the event after a programmatic set calls its handler itself.

records.summary: Modal lifecycle events are modal:*.

records.manual: Replace the option with an addEventListener call for the event named in to.

records.summary: A button without fill or border is the link appearance.

Pin a Pro release whose lock (simai/ui-pro contracts/releases/pro-<12>.lock.json) names, in requires.framework, the free release the page pins (ui-<12>), and serve both from those releases; ui-09bc6b371eca is the first free release without the four components, pro-1f894a46f488 the Pro release built against it. The record is removed, not compat, because there is no alias to sweep: the free release dropped the components at once, and the Pro package carries them unchanged. deprecated_on and remove_after are the policy's dates for the day of the move and mean nothing further here. sf-upgrade reports a use of the four tags only in a project that declares no Pro package. records.manual: sf-upgrade --apply rewrites a declaration of a format: in a JSON file that keeps the standard layout (JSON.stringify with two or four spaces, or tabs), every "schema": "simai.<name>.v<major>" becomes "schema": "simai.<name>" with "schema_version": <major> right after it; in a script, a literal schema: 'simai.<name>.v<major>' (or 'schema' => '...' in PHP) gains schema_version beside it when the file names schema_version nowhere else. What it reports and leaves: a comparison against the label (a reader of your own: read both forms until remove_after with readSchema or isSchema from core/js/composition/schema-name.mjs), a JSON file in another layout, and every format an item marks held -- the Framework itself keeps those in the older form for the reason given, so leave them until the item is released.

records.summary: A composition value type is named without a version: record-changed, record-removed, collection-changed, files-moved, counter, navigation, preference-changed, record-id, record-ids, text and boolean, in place of the older labels record-changed.v1 and the rest. Both forms are read until remove_after, so a host, a component and a page may move one at a time; a route between a bare name and its older label already works.

records.summary: SF.Effects.EFFECT_SCHEMA held the older label of the effect format, simai.effect.v1, and was described as the label a writer emits, against format-names-without-version. A writer now spreads SF.Effects.EFFECT_FORMAT, {schema: 'simai.effect', schema_version: 1}, into an effect.json. EFFECT_SCHEMA keeps its value until remove_after, so a writer that put it alone in "schema" still writes a manifest every reader takes; reading it through SF.Effects is noted in SF.deprecations. records.manual: Where code writes {schema: SF.Effects.EFFECT_SCHEMA, ...} (or imports EFFECT_SCHEMA from core/js/effects.js), write {...SF.Effects.EFFECT_FORMAT, ...}. A comparison against the label is a reader: use isSchema(manifest, 'simai.effect', 1) from core/js/composition/schema-name.mjs, or SF.Effects.checkEffectManifest.

records.summary: The size ladder decides a spinner's geometry (simai/ui-source#10): at each step, 1/3 to 3, its diameter is the icon of an sf-button of the same size and its stroke that icon's stroke. records.summary: The class unit ajax is removed. It was one re-export of the legacy system's SF.Ajax helper, built as a second copy that no Loader rule loaded and nothing imported.

records.manual: Load the content with fetch() when the element enters the viewport (an IntersectionObserver), or use the Smart component sf-include (src, load="view"), which ships in the same pair; sf-fragment is the core's fragment boundary, not a loader. [sf-canceltrack] has no successor: an observer stops by itself after the first load. Bitrix sites keep their own frozen copy of the unit. deprecated_on and remove_after are the policy's dates for the day of the removal and mean nothing further: no Loader rule ever loaded the unit, so there was no alias to keep.

records.summary: The SIMAI Framework Pro component package (sf-table, sf-data-view, sf-property-view, sf-admin-menu and the rest built from simai/ui-pro) is named pro, not larena; Larena is one of its consumers. The Loader takes the old name as a dated alias until remove_after: SF_BOOT_CONFIG.packages.larena declares the same package as packages.pro (the same base, the same rule file), and a package built under the old name, whose rule file calls SF.RuleLoader.registerPackage('larena', ...), registers as pro. Each use is noted in SF.deprecations. When a page declares both names, pro is used and larena is said aloud and ignored. The tags, rules, attributes, events and ports are unchanged.
records.manual: Write pro for larena in the page's package declaration (SF_BOOT_CONFIG.packages.pro, or 'packages' => ['pro' => [...]] in a PHP config) and take a package built as pro (pro-<12>, package-pro.tar, wave-1/output/package/pro): its rule file calls registerPackage('pro'). The base may stay where it is served. A Framework pair from before this record knows only the name the page declares, so a page and the package it loads move together: either both say larena (an older pair) or the page says pro over this pair or later, where both builds work.

records.summary: The background system's naming scheme (C16, owner-approved 2026-11-08; role, variant, state): 51 theme roles take purpose names -- surface-0 and surface-1 are surface-page and surface-area, elevation-1/3/4--surface are surface-card, surface-popup and surface-popup-nested (their shadows and dim ink likewise), <colour>-transparent-hover/select/active are <colour>-state-*, <colour>-transparent-overlay is <colour>-container-strong, surface-overlay is surface-veil, outline-<colour> is <colour>-outline, disable and on-disable are surface-disabled and on-surface-disabled. Values do not change: each former name is var() of its new name, declared on the theme root and on every rule that re-declares the role. Elevation 2 and 5 and the four shadow--* names are held (token-aliases.v1.json, held).

Twenty public component variables that set a fill end in -background-color, as the other 53 do (C16 naming): --sf-card-background is --sf-card-background-color, and so on for alert-bar, code, contents, figure, kbd, list-attention, pager, procedure, progress-run, search, site-header, tile-metric, wizard and workspace-drawer. The component reads the new name first and the former one under it, so a page that sets the former name draws as before.

The background utilities take the C16 names beside the former ones: bg-surface-page, -area, -card, -popup and -popup-nested (the place classes also declare --sf-surface-place and the place's dim ink), bg-<colour>-state-select, bg-<colour>-container-strong, bg-surface-veil, bg-surface-disabled, hover:/active:bg-<colour>-state. The former classes paint the same colour until remove_after.

The shadow system (C20, owner-approved 2026-11-08): four shadows by place -- --sf-shadow-flat, --sf-shadow-raised, --sf-shadow-overlay, --sf-shadow-modal, from --sf-shadow-key-color and --sf-shadow-ambient-color -- replace the numbered levels (--sf-elevation-N--shadow, --sf-ui-shadow-N), the upward layer style and the three shadow colours. Level 1 is raised, 2 and 3 overlay, 4 and 5 modal; the C16 names --sf-shadow-card, -popup and -popup-nested are raised, overlay and overlay. Level 2's and 5's surfaces and dim ink, held by C16, join popup and popup-nested. Each former name is var() of its successor on the theme root; the value follows the place, a visible change approved as C20 (light theme one key and one ambient layer at black 16 and 8, dark theme the key at 28 and no ambient).

The elevation-N classes keep their surface and take their place's shadow.

Coloured shadows go (C20, C17): a shadow carries no colour meaning, and a coloured halo reads as focus or as a status. shadow-<colour>, hover:shadow-<colour>, active:shadow-<colour> and drop-shadow-<colour>, hover:drop-shadow-<colour> colour the key and the ambient shadow of their own element until remove_after, then are removed with no successor. The core rule that gave a shadow to any element with "shadow" in a class ([class*="shadow"], [class*="drop-shadow"]) is gone now: a shadow utility draws its own.

The finding names every spacing option of the constructors it sees: leave the one of an icon button (sf-icon-button), whose spacing is not deprecated.

records.summary: sf-segmented has a height of its own, height="low|default|high|highest" (decision C27, as sf-button): the track stands as tall as an sf-button of the same size and height. spacing, which moved the segments' side padding only, is deprecated: it keeps drawing as before with a console warning until remove_after and is not turned into a height.
records.manual: Remove spacing from the sf-segmented. For a lower or a higher control write height="low", "high" or "highest"; spacing="normal" is the default and is simply removed. spacing changed the sides only, so pick the height the design wants.

records.summary: sf-file-download's seven public variables carry the element's name, not its former tag's (docs pre-check 2026-11-10 DF-11): --sf-download-file-background-color is --sf-file-download-background-color, and so on for -border-color, -radius, -padding, -gap, -icon-size and -icon-color. The class sheet reads the new name first and the former one under it, so a page that sets the former name draws as before.

The class icon button follows decision C15 as the Smart one does (value-icon-button-looks-c15; docs pre-check 2026-11-10, navigation item 2): sf-icon-button--surface is retired and draws as sf-icon-button--tonal with the scheme it is written with, and sf-icon-button--secondary is retired and draws as the quiet neutral, sf-icon-button--on-surface sf-icon-button--on-surface-variant (component.icon-buttons 1.6.0). The alpha-ramp surface look and the secondary container tonal look are gone; the names keep drawing their successors until remove_after.
records.manual: Write sf-icon-button--tonal for sf-icon-button--surface and keep the scheme class. For sf-icon-button--secondary write sf-icon-button--on-surface and sf-icon-button--on-surface-variant: one class becomes two, so it is not a plain rename.

records.summary: The carousel's surface modifiers carry the C16 place names (docs pre-check 2026-11-10, CR-01): sf-carousel-switch--surface-zero is sf-carousel-switch--surface-page and sf-carousel-pagination--surface-2 is sf-carousel-pagination--surface-area (component.carousel 1.2.0). The former classes draw the same until remove_after.

The floating action button's tonal pair is primary (dispatcher decision e, docs pre-check 2026-11-10; C15 retired secondary for the icon buttons): sf-fab--tonal sf-fab--primary draws the primary container under on-primary-container (component.fab 1.1.0). sf-fab--secondary is its former name and draws the same until remove_after.

The clipboard button's size classes carry the size names, as every sized component's do (CP-03, docs pre-check 2026-11-10; component.clipboard 1.1.0): sf-clipboard--size-1/3, sf-clipboard--size-1 and sf-clipboard--size-2 are the control ladder's 1/3, 1 and 2 steps. sf-clipboard-1, -2 and -3 are their former names and draw the same until remove_after.
